scenarios.prompt: Write a TypeScript HTTP handler: parse a user ID from request params, fetch the user from DB (async), check the user has admin role. Each step returns a typed AppError with a code field. Map error codes to HTTP status codes at the end. Do not use exceptions.
criteria: Uses Either with a typed error type that has a code or discriminant field
Uses .bind() / .bindAsync() pipeline instead of try/catch or nested ifs
Uses .match() to map error codes to HTTP status codes at the end

scenarios.prompt: A third-party crypto library exposes hash(data: string): string but throws on invalid input. Write a TypeScript wrapper that returns Either<Error, string> instead of throwing. Also show how to use it in a pipeline.
criteria: Uses Try.run() to capture the throw from the third-party function

Converts the Try to Either with .toEither() (typically followed by .mapLeft() to get an Error) or with a single .match(), not by consuming the lazy Try twice (e.g. .isSuccess() then .onFail()) without .memo()
No bare try/catch block in the wrapper

scenarios.prompt: Write TypeScript: look up a value from Redis cache (returns Either<'miss', CachedValue>). If cache miss (Left), fall back to a DB query (async, also returns Either<'db_error', DbValue>). If DB also misses, return Left. Show the full fallback chain.
criteria: Uses Either.left() (or the equivalent left() function) to represent cache miss and DB miss
Uses .bindLeftAsync() or .bindLeft() to implement the fallback on Left
Chain stops when the first Right is found (does not always go to DB)

scenarios.prompt: Write TypeScript: an order-cancellation flow uses a repository whose methods return T | null: findOrder(id), findCustomer(order.customerId) and findPaymentFor(order.id). Each missing record must become a typed AppError { code: 'ORDER_NOT_FOUND' | 'CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND' | 'PAYMENT_NOT_FOUND'; message: string }, and the flow stops at the first missing record. Do not use exceptions or null checks.
criteria: Converts each nullable result into an Either with toEither(value, error) or Option.from(value).toEither(error) (value or factory), instead of if/null checks
Uses a typed error with a code field for each missing record
Chains the lookups with .bind() (or .bindAsync()) so later lookups do not run after the first Left

scenarios.prompt: Write TypeScript: save a report to disk with fs.writeFileSync(path, contents), which returns nothing and throws on permission or disk errors. Expose saveReport(path, contents) that returns an Either whose error side is AppError { code: 'WRITE_FAILED'; message: string } and whose success side carries no data, so it can be chained with other Either steps. Do not use try/catch.
criteria: Maps the void result to Unit.default with Try's .map() before calling .toEither() (toEither throws on an undefined value)
Maps the error to the WRITE_FAILED AppError with .mapLeft() (or builds it in a single .match()), with no try/catch block
